name: Archival Map Investigation
description: A historical investigation cover: an original period portrait or key artifact, a marked parchment map, and one archival-event strip beneath a precise model-rendered headline.
tagline: Portrait, map, and evidence-led historical reveal

recipe.conceptGuidance: Build an original evidence-led historical investigation cover. Pair one period-appropriate portrait or defining artifact on the left with a parchment map in the upper-right and a narrow archival scene, document, or event strip below it. The frame should promise a careful explanation of how a concrete institution, agreement, route, or policy shaped an outcome.
compositionRules: Place one original period portrait or defining artifact in the left third; never reuse a real channel's crop, identity treatment, logo, or branding.
Place a weathered parchment map in the upper-right with only a few clear route arrows, dots, or boundary marks; preserve a clean visual hierarchy rather than a dense infographic.
Use a narrow lower-right archival-event strip showing a relevant historical setting, document, crowd, ship, rail line, market, or institution.
Reserve the lower-left to lower-middle as a title-safe zone for two to four stacked white headline bands. Render the exact episode title in those bands as bold, readable black uppercase lettering.
Use black, cream, sepia, and restrained oxblood accents; keep the image sober, legible, and mobile-readable.
requiredElements: one period portrait or defining historical artifact
two to four stacked white bands containing the exact episode title
avoid: copied creator trade dress, logos, watermarks, channel names, or recognizable source-thumbnail layouts
unsupported secret plots, ethnic or religious scapegoating, a sole-cause claim, or claims of intentionality not supported by the episode's evidence
sensational accusations, conspiracy imagery, dense labels, illegible map text, placeholder lettering, or post-render headline overlays
more than one competing portrait, excessive arrows, or a crowded undifferentiated collage
recipe.visualStyleGuidance: Original archival editorial collage: high-contrast black-and-cream historical portraiture or artifact study, weathered parchment map, restrained sepia documentary texture, sparse oxblood route marks, and bold white newspaper-like headline bands. Preserve the selected project visual art style as the final rendering authority; do not imitate a specific channel or historical publisher.
